0-NI-1.o: Count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, from any number

0-NI-2.o: Identify and represent numbers using objects and pictures; compare numbers using more than, less than and equal to; read and write numbers to 20 in words

0-NI-3.o: Represent and use number bonds and related subtraction facts within 20; add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20

0-TT-1.o: Count in multiples of twos, fives and tens

0-TT-2.o: Solve one-step multiplication and division problems using objects, pictures and arrays

0-FF-1.o: Recognise, find and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape or quantity

0-FF-2.o: Recognise, find and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape or quantity

0-MM-1.o: Compare, describe and measure lengths and heights

0-MM-2.o: Compare, describe and measure mass/weight and capacity/volume

0-MM-3.o: Recognise and know the value of different coins and notes

0-MM-4.o: Tell the time to the hour and half past the hour

0-SF-3.o: Describe position, direction and movement, including half, quarter and three-quarter turns

0-DD-1.o: Sort and count objects, and compare groups (early data: not statutory until Year 2)

1-NI-1.o: Recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number; compare and order numbers from 0 up to 100

1-NI-2.o: Add and subtract numbers using concrete objects, pictures and mentally, including two-digit numbers and ones/tens

1-NI-3.o: Recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction to check calculations and solve missing number problems

1-TT-1.o: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 2, 5 and 10 multiplication tables

1-TT-2.o: Recognise odd and even numbers; show that multiplication of two numbers can be done in any order (commutative)

1-TT-3.o: Solve problems involving multiplication and division, using materials, arrays, repeated addition and mental methods

1-FF-1.o: Recognise, find, name and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity

1-FF-2.o: Find fractions of amounts; write simple fractions, e.g. 1/2 of 6 = 3

1-MM-1.o: Choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure length/height (m/cm); compare and order lengths

1-MM-2.o: Measure mass (kg/g), temperature (°C) and capacity (litres/ml); compare and order

1-MM-3.o: Recognise and use symbols for pounds/pence (here: dirhams/fils); find combinations of coins; solve problems including giving change

1-MM-4.o: Tell and write the time to five minutes, including quarter past/to the hour

1-SF-1.o: Identify and describe the properties of 2-D shapes, including the number of sides and line symmetry

1-SF-2.o: Identify and describe the properties of 3-D shapes, including the number of edges, vertices and faces

1-SF-3.o: Use mathematical vocabulary to describe position, direction and movement, including turns

1-DD-1.o: Interpret and construct simple tally charts and tables; ask and answer questions by totalling and comparing

1-DD-2.o: Interpret and construct simple pictograms and block diagrams

2-NI-1.o: Recognise the place value of each digit in a three-digit number; compare, order, read and write numbers up to 1000; find 10 or 100 more or less

2-NI-2.o: Add and subtract numbers mentally, including a three-digit number and ones, tens or hundreds

2-NI-3.o: Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using formal written methods; estimate the answer and use inverse operations to check

2-TT-1.o: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4 and 8 multiplication tables

2-TT-2.o: Write and calculate multiplication and division using known facts, including two-digit × one-digit, mentally and with written methods

2-TT-3.o: Solve problems, including missing number problems, scaling problems and correspondence problems

2-FF-1.o: Count up and down in tenths; recognise, find and write fractions of a discrete set of objects

2-FF-2.o: Recognise and show, using diagrams, equivalent fractions with small denominators

2-FF-3.o: Compare and order unit fractions and fractions with the same denominators; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole

2-MM-1.o: Measure, compare, add and subtract lengths (m/cm/mm); measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes

2-MM-2.o: Measure, compare, add and subtract mass (kg/g) and volume/capacity (l/ml)

2-MM-3.o: Add and subtract amounts of money to give change

2-MM-4.o: Tell and write the time from an analogue clock, including 12-hour and 24-hour clocks; estimate and compare time

2-SF-1.o: Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn; identify right angles and whether angles are greater or less than a right angle

2-SF-2.o: Identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines; draw 2-D shapes and make 3-D shapes

2-DD-1.o: Interpret and present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables; solve one-step and two-step questions

3-NI-1.o: Recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number; order and compare numbers beyond 1000; round any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000

3-NI-2.o: Add and subtract numbers with up to 4 digits using the formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction

3-TT-1.o: Recall multiplication and division facts for multiplication tables up to 12 × 12

3-TT-2.o: Use place value, known and derived facts to multiply and divide mentally; recognise and use factor pairs and commutativity

3-TT-3.o: Multiply two-digit and three-digit numbers by a one-digit number using formal written layout; solve problems

3-FF-1.o: Recognise and show families of common equivalent fractions; solve problems to calculate quantities and fractions to divide quantities

3-FF-2.o: Recognise and write decimal equivalents of any number of tenths or hundredths; round decimals with one decimal place to the nearest whole number

3-FF-3.o: Recognise and write decimal equivalents to 1/4, 1/2, 3/4; compare numbers with the same number of decimal places; solve simple money problems

3-MM-1.o: Measure and calculate the perimeter of a rectilinear figure; find the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares

3-MM-2.o: Convert between different units of measure, e.g. kilometre to metre, hour to minute

3-MM-3.o: Estimate, compare and calculate different measures, including money in pounds and pence (here: dirhams and fils)

3-MM-4.o: Read, write and convert time between analogue and digital 12- and 24-hour clocks

3-SF-1.o: Identify acute and obtuse angles and compare and order angles up to two right angles; compare and classify geometric shapes

3-SF-2.o: Identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes presented in different orientations

3-SF-3.o: Describe positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant; describe movements between positions as translations

3-DD-1.o: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using bar charts and time graphs; solve comparison, sum and difference problems

4-NI-1.o: Read, write, order and compare numbers to at least 1 000 000; interpret negative numbers in context; round any number up to 1 000 000

4-NI-2.o: Add and subtract whole numbers with more than 4 digits, including using formal written methods, and mentally with increasingly large numbers

4-TT-1.o: Identify multiples and factors, including all factor pairs and common factors; know and use prime numbers

4-TT-2.o: Recognise and use square numbers and cube numbers, and the notation for squared (²) and cubed (³)

4-TT-3.o: Multiply and divide whole numbers and those involving decimals by 10, 100 and 1000

4-TT-4.o: Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a one- or two-digit number using a formal written method; divide numbers up to 4 digits by a one-digit number

4-FF-1.o: Identify, name and write equivalent fractions; recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions and convert from one form to the other

4-FF-2.o: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator and denominators that are multiples of the same number; multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers

4-FF-3.o: Read, write, order and compare numbers with up to three decimal places; round decimals with two decimal places

4-FF-4.o: Recognise the per cent symbol and understand per cent as parts per hundred; write percentages as a fraction and a decimal

4-MM-1.o: Convert between different units of metric measure

4-MM-2.o: Measure and calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes; calculate and compare the area of rectangles

4-MM-3.o: Estimate volume (e.g. using 1 cm³ blocks) and capacity

4-MM-4.o: Solve problems involving converting between units of time

4-SF-1.o: Know angles are measured in degrees; estimate and compare acute, obtuse and reflex angles; angles at a point and on a straight line

4-SF-2.o: Use the properties of rectangles to deduce related facts and find missing lengths and angles; distinguish regular and irregular polygons

4-SF-3.o: Identify, describe and represent the position of a shape following a reflection or translation

4-DD-1.o: Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information presented in a line graph; complete, read and interpret information in tables, including timetables

5-NI-1.o: Read, write, order and compare numbers up to 10 000 000; round any whole number; use negative numbers in context and calculate intervals across zero

5-NI-2.o: Perform mental calculations, including with mixed operations and large numbers; use estimation to check answers

5-TT-1.o: Multiply multi-digit numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit number using long multiplication; divide using long division

5-TT-2.o: Identify common factors, common multiples and prime numbers

5-TT-3.o: Use their knowledge of the order of operations to carry out calculations involving the four operations

5-FF-1.o: Use common factors to simplify fractions; compare and order fractions, including fractions > 1

5-FF-2.o: Add and subtract fractions with different denominators and mixed numbers; multiply simple pairs of proper fractions; divide proper fractions by whole numbers

5-FF-3.o: Identify the value of each digit in numbers given to three decimal places; multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000; use written division methods with decimal answers

5-FF-4.o: Recall and use equivalences between simple fractions, decimals and percentages, including in different contexts

5-MM-1.o: Use, read, write and convert between standard units; convert between miles and kilometres

5-MM-2.o: Calculate the area of parallelograms and triangles; recognise when it is possible to use formulae for area

5-MM-3.o: Calculate, estimate and compare volume of cubes and cuboids using standard units

5-SF-1.o: Find unknown angles in any triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons; recognise vertically opposite angles

5-SF-2.o: Illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter and circumference; recognise, describe and build simple 3-D shapes, including making nets

5-SF-3.o: Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants); draw and translate simple shapes and reflect them in the axes

5-DD-1.o: Interpret and construct pie charts and line graphs and use these to solve problems

5-DD-2.o: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average

5-PP-1.o: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities, ratio and proportion, and scale factors

5-PP-2.o: Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages and the use of percentages for comparison

5-PP-3.o: Use simple formulae; generate and describe linear number sequences

5-PP-4.o: Express missing number problems algebraically; find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns
